card.title: Lens maker formula — grinding glass into focus

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A lens is two spherical refracting surfaces back to back. Its focal length is manufactured in: flatter curves or lower index → weaker lens. Converging (convex) lenses form real images of real objects; diverging (concave) give only virtual ones. Power (dioptre = 1/m) adds in contact combinations. Angular magnification is the ratio of visual angles with and without the instrument.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: maker: 1/f = (μ − 1)·(1/R₁ − 1/R₂)  ·  lens: 1/f = 1/v − 1/u (Cartesian)  ·  m = v/u  ·  power P = 1/f(m) in dioptre; contact: P = P₁ + P₂  ·  symmetric biconvex R: 1/f = (μ−1)·2/R

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Thin-lens + paraxial approximations throughout; thick lenses shift principal planes. Sign convention fixed once (Cartesian: light left→right, R positive if centre is on the outgoing side). Maker formula assumes the lens sits in air — immerse it and (μ−1) becomes (μ_rel − 1).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Equiconvex glass (μ = 1.5): 1/f = 0.5·2/R → f = R — focal length equals the radius, a beloved shortcut. Plano-convex halves the power (one flat face contributes nothing). f = 15 cm lens imaging 2× real: 1/v − 1/u with m = v/u = −2 → u = −22.5 cm, v = −45 cm (NEB 2023).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: f = 15 cm convex, real image twice the object: m = v/u = −2 → v = −2u. Lens formula 1/15 = 1/(−2u) − 1/u = −3/2u → u = −22.5 cm, v = −45 cm — object 22.5 cm out, image 45 cm out, inverted, doubled (NEB 2023, 4 marks; signs in Cartesian).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Real lenses carry chromatic aberration (μ varies with colour — next unit's problem) and spherical aberration (marginal rays focus short). The maker formula designs focal length, not image quality. Contact-power addition ignores inter-lens separation.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Refract through the first spherical surface (n₂/v − n₁/u = (n₂−n₁)/R), feed its image as the object of the second surface with sign care, thin-lens limit (thickness → 0): the intermediate distances cancel leaving 1/f = (μ−1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂) — the NEB 5-marker for a convex lens.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Power in dioptre = 100/f(cm). Converging = positive f, diverging = negative. 'Derive for convex lens' → write the two-surface refraction chain, don't memorise the end. Real-image questions: m negative, v and u same sign side.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2022 (5): state + derive the thin lens maker's formula for a convex lens. NEB 2023 (4): f = 15 cm, real 2× image — object and image positions. Power/combination and magnification numericals rotate yearly.
